title: Calderón Planned That in 2030 Mexican-Americans Would Govern Our Country
author: Nancy Flores
content:
_This article by[Nancy
Flores](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/nancy_contra/) originally appeared
in the [September 22, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/calderon-planeo-que-
en-2030-mexicoamericanos-gobernaran-nuestro-pais/), a Mexican investigative
journalism magazine._

_After the electoral fraud of July 2006, Felipe Calderón devised a trans-
sexennial plan he called “Mexico 2030. Grand Vision Project,” in which he
outlined the route for the total surrender of the country to US interests.
Chapter 5 proposes that our nation would be governed by “Mexican-Americans”
and will have been “integrated” into North America. The objectives: public
policies dictated directly from the United States, the creation of “shared
institutions,” subordination of the Mexican Armed Forces so that they would
intervene in international conflicts for “hemispheric security,” thereby
abandoning the principle of non-intervention. In addition, it established a
route to abandon the concept of “sovereignty.” According to that Calderón
plan, the country 's development should not be of the BRIC type (Brazil,
Russia, India, China). Now, President Sheinbaum is promoting an initiative to
prevent persons with dual nationality from reaching the Presidency of the
Republic, which today was approved in general by the majority in the Chamber
of Deputies._

Three months after the 2006 electoral fraud and when he had already received
the certificate accrediting him as president-elect, the PAN member Felipe de
Jesús Calderón Hinojosa, together with PRIAN politicians, right-wing
intellectuals and communicators, as well as supposed members of “organized
civil society,” outlined a document called _Mexico 2030, Grand Vision
Project_. That plan established a route for the total surrender of the country
to transnational interests, in particular to US ones.

In its last chapter, “Axis 5. Effective Democracy and Responsible Foreign
Policy,” the document in the possession of _Contralínea_ highlights that among
the objectives for Mexican foreign policy was the aspiration that by 2030
**“some Mexican-Americans” would hold “relevant public positions in certain
areas,”** as part of the “process of integration with North America.”

![Page from Felipe Calderón's “Mexico 2030, Grand Vision Project”
document](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/02-mexico-2030-doc-1.png)

The route for people born in the United States to begin governing Mexico was
to start with positions related to the “financial, commercial and public
policy areas.” With this, supposedly, the country would achieve a
“consolidated leadership.”

The plan is especially relevant now that the Congress of the Union is
discussing the reform initiative sent by President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo so
that people who aspire to govern Mexico or its federal entities do not have
dual nationality, and which on the afternoon of this September 22 was approved
in general in the Chamber of Deputies.

![Page from Felipe Calderón's “Mexico 2030, Grand Vision Project”
document](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/03-mexico-2030-doc-2.png)

Asked this morning by _Contralínea_ about the PAN's surrender to foreign
interests, and in particular about this plan by Felipe Calderón, President
Sheinbaum commented that in the coming days she will review that information
and even make it public at the morning press conference. In addition, she
questioned the opposition that refuses to legislate so that there are no
people with two nationalities in the Presidency of the Republic and in state
governments.

“In the Constitution it was established that to be president […] your parents
had to be –both of them– Mexican: mother and father. Later, the Constitution
was changed so that one of the two could be born in another country. But
beyond who your parents are –which ultimately you don't decide–, you, as a
Mexican, now to run, the issue is: to whom do you owe yourself? Do you have
two flags? Do you have two homelands? No, you only have one, because you are
the highest representation of Mexico. So, it is incomprehensible [why they
don't want to vote for it]. Because it is not taking away any right from
anyone, it is only if you are going to run for president or for governor.”

> You can only have one master, and that is the people of Mexico.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

## Calderón's Plan

The resistance of the opponents, especially the PRIAN, is explained by their
own history of surrender to foreign interests, and especially by the
neoliberal politicians who have systematically favored the interests of the
United States. An example of this is precisely Felipe Calderón's so-called
“Grand Vision Project,” which also established that the country will be “a
fundamental part of a North American community, encompassing Mexico, the
United States and Canada.”

The document –made in the context of the thematic workshops convened by the
PAN member Calderón Hinojosa in October 2006, amid social discontent over the
imposition of his future government– added that this “North American
community” will be “integrated with shared policies and institutions,
including a common security space and a deep relationship in matters of
migration, trade and investment.”

The document –which was originally classified as confidential and later
declassified by the Calderón government– proposed abandoning the conception of
sovereignty: “**Concepts considered ‘sacrosanct,’ such as sovereignty, must be
reconsidered** , since they trigger debates that may come to contaminate the
country's international agenda.”

![Page from Felipe Calderón's “Mexico 2030, Grand Vision Project”
document](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/04-mexico-2030-doc-3.png)

## Military Annexation

The file _Mexico 2030, Grand Vision Project_ consists of 14 documents totaling
831 pages. Originally classified as confidential, they contain the results of
the thematic workshops convened by the PAN member Felipe de Jesús Calderón in
October 2006, after being declared president-elect of Mexico by the Electoral
Tribunal of the Federal Judiciary and in the midst of the post-electoral
crisis.

These workshops were sponsored by the Trust to Support the Change of
Administration of the Federal Executive and were divided into five axes: 1)
rule of law and public security; 2) competitive and job-generating economy; 3)
equal opportunities; 4) sustainable development; 5) effective democracy and
responsible foreign policy.

In its note “xvi,” corresponding to the chapter “Axis 5. Effective Democracy
and Responsible Foreign Policy,” the document reveals that the Calderón plan
–accompanied by those who also backed the electoral fraud– sought for **the
Army and the Navy to participate in invasions and international conflicts**.
By agreeing in the workshops on the “vision” that Mexico will be “a country
with leading armed forces that contribute to consolidating hemispheric
leadership,” the authors of the plan agreed that “the role of the Army would
not be limited to its intervention in conflict situations, since its
collaboration was also very valuable in other non-belligerent situations, such
as natural disasters.”

Another point of interest revealed by Calderón's _Grand Vision Project_ is
that, by 2030, Mexico would be “a very active country in the international
military security system, in order to be heard by other international actors
of great weight”; it will share “security zones and perimeters in the
hemisphere,” and will be a “middle power” with military capacity to “defend
the world and its interests.”

In the military sphere, the objective was also pursued that our country be “a
very influential actor in defining the hemispheric agenda,” and that it be a
“promoter of conflict resolution and driver of priority issues, especially
that of security.”

## 2030 Plan Rejected the Then-BRIC

In defining the type of relations that Mexico should establish with the world
in that Calderón vision, the document dedicated to foreign policy not only
prioritized the link with North America, but rejected BRIC-type development
(Brazil, Russia, India and China). In addition, it marginalized the
relationship with Latin America, by limiting it to five countries. At the same
time, it emphasized its “interest” in Cuba.

By 2030, this will be “**a developed non-BRIC country** , with migratory flows
toward Mexico which has ceased to be a labor-expelling country” (_sic_), the
document indicates.

![Page from Felipe Calderón's “Mexico 2030, Grand Vision Project”
document](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/05-mexico-2030-doc-4.png)

And it adds that, by 2030, Mexico would be “a country with a strategic
relationship with four or five countries of South America.” In addition, among
the factors inhibiting the plan, it identified that in Latin America there are
personalized and populist leaderships of the past, in reference to the then-
presidents Raúl Castro, of Cuba; Hugo Chávez, of Venezuela; and Evo Morales,
of Bolivia. The references to Cuba go further: “To be part of and be a leader
of the economic community of North and Central America, especially Cuba.”

Another point that stands out is that it said goodbye to Mexico's non-
interventionist tradition. This, because one of the objectives of the plan
_Mexico 2030, Grand Vision Project_ is that Mexicans forget their non-
interventionist past, to transition toward “a country with a positive
projection toward North America, with a 21st-century foreign policy capable of
facing globalization, which has overcome the 20th-century foreign policy that
in its time was effective in facing the Cold War.”

document](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
